core.title: REFACTOR only after GREEN, guided by the refactor sensors
core.given: a governed ATDD task whose current behavioral acceptance has passed for the first time (behavioral GREEN)
core.when: you change code to improve its design, including in response to a refactor-sensor finding
core.then: Start REFACTOR only after behavioral GREEN. Keep the now-green behavior fixed, and address refactor-sensor findings one at a time by following each finding's Diagnose / Prefer / Avoid / Verify guidance.
prefer: The refactor sensors are the governed quality-metric sensor rules of the active conventions; the stack realization enumerates them, and each of their findings carries smell-specific guidance.
Address one finding at a time, using that finding's smell-specific Diagnose / Prefer / Avoid / Verify guidance.
Treat each finding as evidence of a design smell, not as the design objective. Fix the smell, not the number.
These sensors may run at any time and stay strict. The phase changes your response, not the validator.
avoid: Starting REFACTOR before the acceptance has passed for the first time.
Forcing a sensor violation just to keep a ceremonial phase boundary.
unless: If a refactor sensor is already satisfied by the smallest correct implementation, keep that result.
core.why: GREEN and REFACTOR are different search problems, and splitting them does not change enforcement. REFACTOR uses the refactor-sensor findings as guided design sensors while preserving the behavior GREEN established.
evidence: REFACTOR changes happen after the acceptance first passed. The acceptance still passes, and no new behavior was added.
Each addressed sensor finding is cleared by a design change, not by gaming the metric.
verification: Term refactor_sensor: a quality finding whose metric is evidence of a design smell rather than the design objective itself; the concrete sensor rules are named by the stack realization, not by this core.
The sensors may run at any time and remain strict. The phase distinction changes the agent's response, not the validator.
The finding fact is context only: the obligation also applies when no refactor-sensor finding is open.
Whether a change adds behavior or games a metric needs judgement; it is not mechanically checkable.

fires: The acceptance has just passed and the agent is improving the design.
A refactor sensor reports a finding after behavioral GREEN.
doesNotFire: The acceptance is still RED. The GREEN part applies instead.
Work with no behavioral acceptance under the governed ATDD loop.

bunOnly.reason: The 'Bun' profile tag scopes the rule to its realization; the core cannot name a stack. Instantiating the core as the Bun realization restores the scoping.

bunOnly.text: The refactor sensors are the bun_ts_metrics_detector rules: coder.bun.complexity-cyclomatic, coder.bun.complexity-length, coder.bun.complexity-nesting, coder.bun.dead-code-reachability, coder.bun.duplication-intra-layer, coder.bun.quality-comments, coder.bun.quality-mi.
bunOnly.reason: Detector and rule ids are realization details (see notProfileKeys); which rules act as refactor sensors differs per stack, and rule ids are rules-corpus data, not structure-profile data.

bunOnly.text: In the Bun coder profile these are the seven bun_ts_metrics_detector rules: complexity-cyclomatic, complexity-length, complexity-nesting, dead-code-reachability, duplication-intra-layer, quality-comments, quality-mi.

neutralityNotes: This convention is process-level and was almost fully neutral already; the core is essentially bun.json minus the realization's sensor enumeration. The only non-neutral content is the concrete refactor-sensor set (detector id bun_ts_metrics_detector plus the seven coder.bun.* rule ids) in prefer[0], verifier_detail[0] and activation.facts[3], and the 'Bun' profile tag in given; these stay in bunOnly because rule/finding/detector ids are realization data (notProfileKeys), they are rules-corpus data rather than structure-profile data, and the sensor set differs per stack, so no vocabulary key fits and none is proposed. The core needs no structure-profile data (it names no role, path, suffix, URN, idiom or tool), hence profileRequirements is empty. 'Diagnose / Prefer / Avoid / Verify' is kept in the core: it is the conventions corpus's own guidance-field structure, not a stack construct. ATDD, GREEN, REFACTOR, RED are treated as stack-neutral loop vocabulary. The activation fact notes (gate / hint only / context only / needs judgement) could not be carried verbatim because the core fact schema has no note field; their semantics are preserved in doesNotFire, verification[2] and verification[3], and in classification notes.
